text: Fill in each blank with the correct term from the sections on pyruvate dehydrogenase and the TCA cycle.
questions: Deficiency of *thiamine/thiamin/vitamin B1:Which B vitamin provides the coenzyme TPP?* impairs both pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, causing lactic acidosis.
The pyruvate dehydrogenase reaction is *irreversible*, so acetyl-CoA cannot be used for net glucose synthesis.
*Isocitrate dehydrogenase/isocitrate dehydrogenase* is the rate-limiting enzyme of the TCA cycle, activated by ADP and inhibited by ATP.
Succinyl-CoA synthetase produces *GTP/guanosine triphosphate* by substrate-level phosphorylation in the TCA cycle.
Arsenite poisons PDH and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase by binding *lipoic acid/lipoate*.

overallFeedback.feedback: PDH requires five coenzymes: TPP (B1), CoA (B5), FAD (B2), NAD⁺ (B3), and lipoate; thiamine deficiency (commonest in alcoholism) causes Wernicke encephalopathy by stalling PDH. The TCA cycle's rate-limiting step at isocitrate dehydrogenase is energy-sensitive, and its sole substrate-level phosphorylation at succinyl-CoA synthetase yields GTP.
